Transmission also occurs via contaminated objects such as clothing, towels, and bedding, and through respiratory secretions in close proximity. The advisory emphasizes vigilance and notes Mpox is not limited to sexual transmission; individuals with suspicious lesions or recent exposure should seek timely diagnosis. Published 2026-11-07.

article.articleHeadline: Zambia: a partnership with China to locally produce a cholera vaccine.
article.articleSummary:
- Cholera vaccine production in Zambia moves closer to local supply as Industrial Development Corporation (IDC) of Zambia and China's Jijia (Beijing) International Medical Technology sign a joint venture to form ZAMVAX Limited to build a cholera vaccine manufacturing unit in the Lusaka South Special Economic Zone. The initial investment of 24.13 million USD will finance the first phase, which will fill, finish, package and quality-control oral cholera vaccines from imported antigens, with full local production of antigens planned in a later phase. The plant targets up to 20 million doses per year. Ownership is 60% IDC and 40% Jijia. The project includes technology transfer and training for Zambian workers, with aims to expand to pediatric and veterinary vaccines subject to feasibility and re
- China to build a cholera vaccine production plant in Zambia's Lusaka-South Economic Zone to cut dependence on imports and potentially supply other African nations. Zambia's 2023-2024 cholera outbreak recorded over 20,000 cases and nearly 700 deaths. The plant will include a bottling and packaging line for oral cholera vaccines, with capacity up to 20 million doses per year, split 50% for Zambia and 50% for export pending regulatory approvals. Future expansion could add pediatric and veterinary vaccines, subject to financing and regulatory clearances. The project supports the African Union's goal of producing 60% of Africa's medicines locally by 2040, addressing ongoing import reliance and the legacy of vaccine shortages during the Covid-19 pandemic.

article.articleHeadline: News | Ituri: James Swan reaffirms MONUSCO's support in the fight against the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: James Swan, the UN Secretary-General's Special Representative in the DRC and head of MONUSCO, reaffirmed on Nov 6 in Bunia MONUSCO's support to the Congolese government in battling the Ebola outbreak in Ituri. Ituri faces two key challenges: ongoing armed-group insecurity and Ebola affecting multiple communities. Swan underscored that civilian protection remains MONUSCO's priority, with intensified blue-helmet presence in Bamande, Irumu, and in certain areas of Djugu. Beyond security, MONUSCO aids the Ebola response by logistics support and by facilitating access for humanitarian and health teams, while securing health facilities and operations in Rwampara and Mongwalu (Djugu), as well as Marabo, Nyakunde, and Niania. He reaffirmed continued collaboration with authorities, humanitarian actors, and communities to protect civilians and strengthen the outbreak response.

article.articleHeadline: Democratic Republic of the Congo: More than 10,000 Ebola cases and 5,000 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached more than 10,000 confirmed cases and 5,000 deaths, according to official data up to November 1, 2026. The outbreak has spread across eight provinces, complicating response efforts and presenting substantial logistical challenges for frontline public health teams in the field. Early detection of cases, provision of appropriate medical care, and thorough contact tracing remain the cornerstones of containment and reducing transmission in affected communities. Health teams are continuing to reach affected areas and to strengthen community awareness about the importance of promptly reporting symptoms and adhering to preventive measures to support containment.

article.articleHeadline: Beni: another nurse carried away by Ebola.
article.articleSummary: As of 7 November 2026, Ebola virus disease continues to claim health workers in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Justin Kataliko, a nurse at Les Bernadins clinic in Beni (North Kivu), died on 5 November 2026. A week earlier, two Congolese doctors died: Safari Samuel on 29 October in Lwemba (Ituri) and Marie-France Shogogo on 28 October at the Ebola Treatment Center in Beni. Samuel, recently graduated, worked in Lwemba and reportedly contracted the illness; about fifteen other people at his facility were ill and had not yet received care. Shogogo, a University of Goma graduate, died after treatment at Beni’s CTE. Earlier, on 10 August 2026, neurosurgeon Charles Mbusa Munyumu died of Ebola at Katwa’s treatment center. Persistent response challenges include shortages of equipment and personal protective gear for health workers.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Madagascar lifts the quarantine for passengers arriving from Nigeria and Kenya.
article.articleSummary: Madagascar lifts quarantine and entry bans for travelers arriving from Kenya and Nigeria as part of revised border health controls amid evolving international Ebola risk. A joint interministerial note, cited by Midi Madagasikara, states that the Ebola import risk from these countries no longer justifies the measures. On arrival, affected passengers must sign a commitment letter issued by air and maritime carriers. A remote telephone follow-up remains for travelers who have stayed or transited in these countries to quickly detect any suspicious symptoms. Travelers from the Democratic Republic of Congo continue under strict border restrictions. Other sanitary controls at all entry points remain in force; non-compliance or misrepresentation can lead to regulatory penalties. Published 7 November 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Response to Ebola in Ituri: the army raises awareness and calls on the soldiers in Bunia not to lower their guard.
article.articleSummary: Despite persistence of Ebola virus disease in Ituri, the Democratic Republic of Congo, the army in Bunia is intensifying prevention efforts. Colonel Emmanuel Libandi, CREC focal point within the FARDC, urged soldiers to maintain strict adherence to barrier measures, stressing that the health of troops sustains operational effectiveness. The briefing notes that military personnel's daily contact with civilians places them at heightened contamination risk, making them a critical link in stopping transmission. Through CREC-led outreach, the objective is to consolidate security forces' involvement in the Ebola response, prevent any relaxation of existing measures, and ensure health protection for both soldiers and nearby communities in the Ituri region. The campaign targets multiple population segments and underscores vigilant public health behavior as essential to national protection.

article.articleHeadline: 30 hippos dead after being poisoned by carbon in a national park in Congo
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Virunga National Park, at least 30 hippopotamuses have died since September from anthrax, caused by Bacillus anthracis; park authorities confirmed the deaths. Anthrax is a zoonotic disease with soil-dwelling spores that can persist for decades, and hippos are particularly susceptible. No new cases have been reported in the past two weeks, but the situation is being closely monitored. Officials believe heavy rainfall may have released the bacterium from the soil. Last year, the park saw at least 50 hippos and other large wildlife killed by anthrax. Local communities have been advised not to touch or consume dead animals and to report them. Virunga National Park, founded in 1925 and spanning about 3,000 square miles, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its active volcanic chain and biodiversity.

article.articleHeadline: "Ebola" knocks on the doors... Libyan ports move immediately and impose strict restrictions on ships arriving from Africa - Libya News 24
article.articleSummary: As of 7 November 2026, Libyan Ports and Maritime Transportation Authority has ordered urgent preventive measures at Libyan harbors to curb spread of infectious diseases such as Ebola and other epidemics, amid outbreaks in Africa including the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, and Nigeria. The rules require pre-notification of ships coming from outbreak countries or those docking at high-risk ports, along with a maritime health declaration and prompt disclosure of any atypical crew symptoms. Port health teams may conduct examinations and testing, with strict enforcement of cleanliness, disinfection, safe waste disposal, and verification of drinking water and onboard food safety. Skippers should be educated on preventive practices and avoid contact with suspected cases except per health guidance. The measures align with International Health Regulations and WHO recommendations, but will not disrupt navigation; each health situation will be assessed independently.

article.articleSummary: Monkeypox cases in Brazil rose in 2026, prompting the Health Ministry to buy up to 20,000 vaccine doses for preventive use. Infectious-disease specialist Dr. Carolina Lázari says mass vaccination isn’t needed yet; priority groups include people living with HIV/AIDS and lab workers handling the virus, with caregivers also at risk. The article recalls 2022’s international emergency with 10,821 Brazilian cases, and 2024’s Congo outbreak driven by variant 1B that led the WHO to declare an ESPII, including child deaths. Rio de Janeiro SES-RJ notes rising cases, with more than 2,000 doses allocated to the city on Nov 4, among 298 confirmed (Jan–Nov 6), 207 in the municipality, zero deaths. In 2025, 119 cases were recorded. article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Ituri: the military governor calls for a general mobilization against the epidemic - LePotentiel
article.articleSummary: On November 6, 2026, the military governor of Ituri Province, General-Major Kasongo Mulumba Batoka Gaby, called for a collective mobilization against the Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak in Ituri, DR Congo. He urged residents to observe health measures, report suspected cases, and cooperate with response teams. The provincial government has strengthened coordination and surveillance, with regular follow-up meetings and guidance to authorities to monitor epidemiology, identify and track contacts, raise community awareness, and mobilize resources to interrupt transmission. He lauded the response teams and urged continued professionalism. Six preventive measures were recommended: report suspected cases or unusual deaths; avoid contact with bodily fluids; follow hygiene and health directives; allow safe patient transport and secure burial practices; cooperate with response teams and monitor contacts for 21 days; reject rumors and rely on official communications. He condemned hostility toward responders and urged solidarity to end the outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: Hepatitis E found in a third of suspected yellow fever cases in the DRC
article.articleSummary: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) seroprevalence is substantial among patients suspected of yellow fever in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). A nationwide retrospective cross-sectional study of 2,007 serum samples from suspected yellow fever cases (2019–2021) found HEV total antibodies in 30.8% (95% CI 28.8–32.8). IgM positivity occurred in 3.6% (n=72); among IgM-positive samples, viral RNA was detected in one (1.4%). Multivariable analysis linked male sex with higher HEV seropositivity (aOR 1.2; 95% CI 1.0–1.5; p=0.028) but lower IgM positivity (aOR 0.6; 95% CI 0.4–1.1; p=0.088). Age 20–29 years showed increased seropositivity (aOR 1.3; 95% CI 1.0–1.8; p=0.046). The study indicates HEV circulation among suspected febrile jaundice patients tested under yellow fever surveillance; less than 5% tested positive for yellow fever, suggesting dual-use screening for other causes. Limitations include retrospective design and population limited to febrile jaundice cases.

article.articleHeadline: Tainan's 17th imported dengue fever case; ill after returning from travel to Vietnam.
article.articleSummary: Taiwan’s Tainan City Health Bureau reports the year’s 17th imported dengue fever case. A woman in her 40s from Yongkang District traveled to Vietnam from October 28 to November 1, returned to Taiwan and initially had no symptoms while working in Kaohsiung. On November 4 she developed fever, headache and body aches; a rapid test on November 5 was positive and laboratory confirmation followed. The case is classified as imported. The dengue prevention center in Tainan notified Kaohsiung City Health Bureau and mobilized emergency fogging, elimination of breeding sources, and indoor/outdoor chemical control to reduce the Aedes mosquito density and the risk of community transmission. Vector surveillance is underway to prevent local transmission, reflecting ongoing dengue vigilance for travelers returning from endemic areas such as Vietnam.

article.articleHeadline: 79% of patients with chronic conditions have their daily activities disrupted when infected with RSV.
article.articleSummary: RSV awareness week (Nov 2–8, 2026) highlights a global GSK survey of 6,041 adults (18+) with chronic conditions across 10 countries, showing RSV infection can markedly disrupt daily life. Among respondents with asthma (52%), COPD (45%), chronic kidney disease (CKD, 35%), cardiovascular disease (29%), and diabetes (27%), symptoms during respiratory infections are reported as more severe. Overall, 36% recover longer than expected, 25% seek primary care, and 18% visit emergency services. For those with prior RSV, 40% describe effects lasting a month or more, and 9% persist beyond a year. Severity remains high: 55% rate symptoms moderate to severe; 68% CKD/COPD, 64% cardiovascular, 63% asthma. In Vietnam, forecasts suggest 4.6 million RSV-related acute respiratory illnesses in adults 60+, with 200,000 hospitalizations and 18,000 related deaths. Yet 79% worry about RSV hindering chronic disease control; 46% haven’t discussed RSV with clinicians in 2 years.

article.articleHeadline: Can Influenza A be transmitted through breast milk?
article.articleSummary: Influenza A infection in Hanoi: A mother tests positive for influenza A (A(H1N1), A(H3N2)); symptoms include fever and cough. Influenza A is an acute respiratory illness spread by droplets; contagious from one day before symptoms to 5–7 days after onset, peaking days 1–3. There is no evidence that seasonal influenza transmits via breast milk; mothers can continue breastfeeding. Breast milk provides antibodies, though the infant remains exposed to droplets or contaminated surfaces. A 4-month-old is high risk for pneumonia, bronchiolitis, otitis media, dehydration, or respiratory failure. Precautions: wear a mask, wash hands for at least 20 seconds before handling the baby or feeding, cover coughs, clean surfaces, ventilate rooms, limit visitors, and avoid face-to-face contact while symptomatic. If needed, expressed milk can be given by a caregiver; antiviral therapy may be started within 48 hours of onset. Seek care for fever, worsening breathing, or dehydration in mother or baby.

article.articleHeadline: A possible source of the illness that afflicted Russian tourists in Vietnam has been named.
article.articleSummary: Russian tourists in Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province, Vietnam report an unknown respiratory illness characterized by high fever and severe cough, affecting many children. Local clinicians have not confirmed a specific pathogen, treating patients with antivirals or antibiotics without a definitive diagnosis. Some travelers suspect air-conditioning–borne microbes; authorities have not released official data on a Khanh Hoa outbreak. Previously, Coxsackie virus infections were reported in Cam Ranh near Nha Trang, with a hotel cluster under observation. Vietnam’s Ministry of Health (Jan–Aug 2026) logged about 100,000 enterovirus infections, roughly 2.5 times higher than the same period last year, with children under five accounting for more than 87%. The hardest-hit regions include Ho Chi Minh City, Dong Nai, Dong Thap, Tay Ninh, Lam Dong, Da Nang, and Hanoi. The report provides no laboratory confirmation or details on imported/exported cases.

article.articleHeadline: Rospotrebnadzor requested data from Vietnam due to the illness of Russian tourists.
article.articleSummary: Rospotrebnadzor (Russia’s consumer health watchdog) asked the Association of Tour Operators (ATOP) and sent a letter to Vietnam’s Ministry of Health over illnesses among Russian tourists in Nha Trang. The agency requested official information on the epidemiological situation, preventive measures, and how information is conveyed to travelers to the Republic of Vietnam. To prevent enteroviral infections, Rospotrebnadzor recommends: regular soap and water handwashing (before meals and after crowded places); drinking only bottled or boiled water and avoiding swallowing pool water; washing fruits and vegetables with boiled or bottled water; minimizing contact with symptomatic individuals; and seeking medical help promptly if health worsens. Previously, Russian tourists reported a “mysterious virus” at Vietnamese resorts, with symptoms like high fever, cough, and severe headache. The report centers on Vietnam and Nha Trang, with Russian travelers affected.

article.articleHeadline: Expert Kapustina: Legionellosis may be the cause of Russians' illness in Vietnam.
article.articleSummary: Russians vacationing in Nha Trang, Vietnam, report fever, cough, and marked weakness; symptoms resemble influenza. While circulating pathogens include influenza A/B, dengue fever, rhinoviruses, adenoviruses, and respiratory syncytial virus, Legionellosis cannot be ruled out, linked to poorly maintained air-conditioning systems. Expert Kapustina recommends early diagnostics: complete blood count to assess inflammation; PCR for influenza and respiratory viruses; serology for dengue and chikungunya; urine antigen for Legionella if suspected. In the early days of illness, tests have the highest diagnostic yield. Prevention emphasizes repellents, sleeping under mosquito nets, and avoiding prolonged exposure in poorly ventilated rooms with constantly running air conditioning; also request hotel information on AC system cleaning. Seek medical care at first signs of illness rather than self-treatment. Rospotrebnadzor has requested Vietnam’s Ministry of Health provide epidemiological data on Russian patients and measures for tourists.

article.articleHeadline: Thirteen contacts identified for the tuberculosis patient working at a kebab shop.
article.articleSummary: Tuberculosis diagnosed in a kebab-shop worker in Latvia triggers contact tracing: 13 contacts identified who spent at least 40 hours with the patient in the past month. Eight study peers and five coworkers/neighbors are under two-year monitoring. The young man was found on the street in serious condition and is hospitalized in Stopiņi and at the Tuberculosis and Lung Diseases Center in Riga. Authorities will follow up with contacts; if symptoms appear, treatment will be provided promptly. The patient has lived in Riga since spring last year; whether the infection was imported remains difficult to determine within a two-year window. Latvia reports 219 TB cases this year, 16 among foreigners; Ukrainians (30), Indians (9), Vietnamese (6) are the largest foreign groups, with others from Lithuania, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Pakistan. TB is airborne; cooking cannot spread it. The Food and Veterinary Service will perform planned kebab-shop inspections twice yearly; no unscheduled checks.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue fever outbreak defies the pattern
article.articleSummary: As of November 7, 2026, Vietnam reports 170,684 dengue cases and 21 deaths in the first 10 months, with the Southern region accounting for 66% of cases. In 2025 Vietnam had 184,903 cases, among the highest in Asia-Pacific. Dengue now circulates year-round across all provinces, breaking the rainfall-driven peak; outbreaks have appeared in previously low-incidence provinces such as Tuyên Quang and Sơn La. Experts note shifts in outbreak cycles: large outbreaks once every five years are shortening to 3–4 years; post-2022 cases remained high. All four dengue serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4) are circulating; serotype dominance varies; vector resistance to insecticides compounds control challenges. The Brazil experience from São Paulo shows a two-dose vaccine reducing symptomatic dengue by 73% and hospitalizations by 87%, with about 24 million doses across 2,752 locales (2024–2025). Vietnamese authorities advocate year-round proactive prevention: vaccination, surveillance, early case detection, vector control, larval/pupal elimination, and bite-avoidance to curb spread.

article.articleHeadline: Federal Government investigates suspected respiratory syndrome in a bird found in Guarujá, on the coast of São Paulo.
article.articleSummary: As of 7 November 2026, Brazil's Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MAPA) is investigating a suspected respiratory and nervous syndrome in a wild Cairina moschata (wild muscovy duck) found in Guarujá, on the coast of São Paulo state, in the Sítio Conceiçãozinha area of the Vicente de Carvalho district. Samples have been collected for laboratory analysis, with results not yet disclosed. The inquiry aims to determine whether avian influenza (bird flu) or Newcastle disease are involved; a suspected case is not a confirmation. Lab confirmation will guide any specific sanitary actions. Surveillance is conducted by agrodefense agencies under standard vigilance protocols. MAPA emphasizes that disease investigations in birds do not by themselves pose a risk to consuming poultry; chicken meat and eggs from officially inspected facilities remain safe.

article.articleHeadline: Votuporanga confirms second case of visceral leishmaniasis in 2026 and issues a public health alert.
article.articleSummary: Votuporanga confirms the second case of visceral leishmaniasis in 2026. A 17-year-old resident of Vila Marim is hospitalized and receiving treatment. The first case of the year occurred in Pozzobon—a 48-year-old man who responded to public-health–provided therapy and is now cured. Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) is caused by Leishmania infantum and damages the liver, spleen, and bone marrow. Symptoms typically appear weeks to months after infection and include prolonged fever, weakness, weight loss, anemia, and abdominal swelling. Transmission occurs via bites from infected female sand flies; urban dogs are common reservoirs. Delayed diagnosis can lead to hemorrhages, immune suppression, secondary infections, and organ failure, with high mortality if untreated. Treatment is free through Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS), enabling cure when started early.

article.articleHeadline: Health vaccinates park rangers in protected areas against yellow fever.
article.articleSummary: Yellow fever vaccination campaign in Paraguay targets park rangers in protected wildlands lacking vaccination, conducted by the Ministry of Public Health with interagency partners (Health Surveillance Directorate, National Vector-borne Diseases Program, PAI, and the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development). Emphasizes pre-travel immunization for areas with virus circulation or risk zones. Yellow fever spreads via urban Aedes aegypti and sylvatic Sabethes and Haemagogus; monkeys are reservoirs and infected mosquitoes transmit the virus to humans entering the jungle. Transmission cycles include urban and sylvatic; the latter occurs in tropical Latin America and Africa. High-risk countries with active circulation include Brazil, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela; Paraguay and Argentina have areas conducive to reactivating sylvatic cycles. Notably, Paraguay experienced a 2008 outbreak in Central Department and rural San Pedro and Caaguazú, with 28 confirmed cases and 11 deaths.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue can cause severe complications and lead to death; learn the warning signs.
article.articleSummary: Brazil projects about 860,000 probable dengue cases in 2027, announced during the Dengue Season Preparation webinar. While not signaling an epidemic at 2024 levels, the prognosis maintains warning about severe disease and death risk. Dengue is a viral illness transmitted by the female Aedes aegypti mosquito, ranging from mild to life-threatening forms with hemorrhages, organ impairment, and circulatory shock. Early recognition of initial symptoms and especially warning signs is essential. Common manifestations include sudden high fever (39–40°C), severe headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pains, fatigue, nausea/vomiting, and a red rash. Not all infections are symptomatic; symptomatic cases typically last 2–7 days, though full recovery may take longer. Alarm signs of severe dengue include intense abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding, dizziness or fainting, marked drowsiness or irritability, and difficulty breathing; any warrant immediate medical evaluation. Severe cases involve plasma leakage, hypotension, and organ failure, increasing mortality risk.

article.articleHeadline: Peru surpasses 100 dengue-related deaths: the figure is on the rise and nearly doubles the 2025 figures.
article.articleSummary: By Oct 31, 2026, dengue caused 101 deaths in Peru, up 94% from the same period in 2025 (52). October accounts for 30% of 2026 fatalities. The north concentrates cases, led by Lambayeque with 25 deaths (Chiclayo province). San Martín and Piura have 17 each; Madre de Dios 9; La Libertad 7; Ucayali 7; Amazonas 5; Lima 4; Loreto and Pasco 3 each; Junín 2; Áncash and Cusco 1 each. Four-week trend (Weeks 40–43) shows 4, 9, 8, 10 deaths, totaling 31 in October, more than double September's 13. Transmission may rise with El Niño 2026's heavy rains. A free dengue vaccination campaign continues in prioritized zones, targeting ages 10–20 to reduce complications and hospitalizations. Access at DNI-required sites in Lima: Hospital San Juan de Lurigancho and centers Campoy, Ganimedes, San Fernando; Carabayllo centers San Pedro de Carabayllo, El Progreso, Raúl Porras Barrenechea.

Infections traced to consumption of artisanal patuá wine produced in the rural area of Óbidos. Municipal Health Secretariat (Semsa) and the state Health Surveillance Department (Sespa) coordinate containment and monitoring, with privacy protections under LGPD. Authorities remain mobilized and seek updates on the six patients and the 24 under monitoring; no further clinical details released.

article.articleHeadline: QC records over 7k dengue cases, holds 3-day activities to "dengue-clustering" area

District 2 reported 2,654 cases; District 5, 1,177; District 4, 974. Children aged 10 and under accounted for 3,201 cases (44%). In response to dengue clustering, the QC Health Department conducted a three-day prevention activity along Margarita Street, Barangay Gulod (3–5 November 2026). District 5 Epidemiology and Surveillance Unit led active case finding, with spraying and fogging by the QCHD Environment and Sanitation Division. article.articleHeadline: Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur among areas that have recovered from ASF
article.articleSummary: ASF in the Philippines’ hog sector shows progress as Ilocos Norte and Ilocos Sur have shifted from red (infected) zones to pink (buffer) or yellow (surveillance) zones per DA-BAI’s National ASF Prevention and Control Program, in Bulletin No. 2026-19 as of October 2026. Red zones denote confirmed outbreaks; pink zones are surrounding buffer areas; yellow zones are adjacent high-risk surveillance areas. Officials urge hog raisers and local authorities to maintain farm biosecurity, regulate movement of live pigs and pork products, and promptly report suspected ASF cases. Past ASF outbreaks severely impacted the hog industry with losses and pork-supply disruptions; ongoing surveillance and biosecurity are intended to sustain recovery. Article published 2026-11-08.

article.articleHeadline: Alert over the new SAT-1 strain of foot-and-mouth disease: how dangerous is it for animals?
article.articleSummary: FMD SAT-1 serotype triggers India alert, though no SAT-1 cases have been reported in India as of November 7, 2026. FMD comprises seven serotypes (O, A, C, SAT-1, SAT-2, SAT-3, Asia-1); immunity to one does not protect against others, and India’s current vaccine does not guard against SAT-1, raising outbreak risk if introduced. SAT-1 has been detected in China and Mongolia, prompting heightened vigilance. Symptoms in cattle, buffalo, goats, sheep, and pigs include high fever, mouth, tongue, gums, and hoof lesions, lameness, and reduced feed intake; mortality may occur in young animals. Transmission occurs via direct contact and via contaminated feed, water, utensils, vehicles, and footwear. Preparatory measures included Bengaluru’s two-day Vajra-SAT exercise with ICAR-NIVEDI, involving 83 representatives from 25 states and 3 Union Territories, focusing on rapid detection, lab confirmation, movement controls, and rapid response. Farmers are advised to isolate suspected animals and consult a veterinarian promptly.

article.articleHeadline: The risk of influenza and viral pneumonia is rising rapidly; Bhopal on alert; do not ignore these symptoms.
article.articleSummary: As of 7 November 2026, AIIMS Bhopal warns of rapidly spreading influenza activity and other respiratory viruses in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, risking pneumonia and serious breathing difficulties. Key symptoms include sudden high fever, chills, headache, body pains, sore throat, cough, and extreme fatigue. Elderly individuals, young children, pregnant women, and smokers, along with those with asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, heart disease, or weakened immunity, face higher risk of severe illness. Prevention stresses annual influenza vaccination and, where appropriate, pneumonia vaccination; wear masks in crowded, poorly ventilated spaces; perform hand hygiene; cover coughs/sneezes; maintain good indoor ventilation; avoid smoking and indoor pollution. Seek urgent medical care for persistent high fever, shortness of breath, chest pain, confusion, or blue lips. Antibiotics are ineffective against viral infections and should be used only under physician guidance.

article.articleHeadline: Girl dies from a dog bite in Surajpur, Chhattisgarh; this is the second such incident in a week.
article.articleSummary: Two-year-old Neerja died at Medical College Hospital, Surajpur district, Chhattisgarh, 10 days after a stray dog bite in Kalyaanpur Gehlapara (Jaynagar area); initial treatment and anti-rabies vaccination were given, but she deteriorated and died, the hospital’s second dog-bite fatality in a week. Earlier, a woman from Navadhakki village in the Pratappur area died after a dog bite, developing rabies symptoms days later. The spate of deaths highlights risks from stray dogs and concerns over rabies vaccine availability and child safety across Surguja division. Expert Dr. CK Mishra advises: immediately wash the wound with running water and soap for at least 15 minutes, avoid home remedies, and seek immediate care for anti-rabies vaccination with a full course; deeper wounds may require anti-rabies serum around the wound, and interrupting vaccination is dangerous as rabies can be fatal if untreated.

article.articleHeadline: Two more children of a school test positive for shigellosis in Keralam's Kozhikode
article.articleSummary: Shigellosis outbreak in Kozhikode, Keralam, linked to Meppayil Senior Basic School. Two more children from Meppayil Senior Basic School have been diagnosed; the three admitted to Government District Hospital are aged 7, 8 and 10, with initial tests negative and all three now testing positive by blood assays. Affected children presented with vomiting, fever and diarrhoea; onset began last Friday, with 104 people reporting similar symptoms over Saturday to Monday. Those affected had eaten egg curry and curd as part of school lunch. Public health teams from health and education departments, led by the District Medical Officer, inspected the school. Health workers visited 950 homes to distribute oral rehydration salts (ORS); wells at 290 properties were chlorinated as a precaution. The outbreak response emphasizes food handling and water sanitation in the school community.

article.articleHeadline: AIIMS Deoghar trains 235 health workers in TB detection

Dean (Research) Prof Somashekhar Nimbalkar said strengthening diagnostic capacity at the grassroots level is essential for improving health outcomes, and the program aims to bridge the gap between primary healthcare services and specialized diagnostic facilities. article.articleHeadline: Bijnor reports 4,500 Hepatitis C cases, twice last year's count
article.articleSummary: Bijnor district in Uttar Pradesh reports over 4,500 Hepatitis C cases this year, more than double the nearly 2,000 tallied in 2025. About 55,000 samples have been tested to date, with nearly 16 patients presenting daily at three government treatment centers, mainly from rural areas. Health officials say increased testing and ongoing awareness programs partly explain the rise. Hepatitis C is a viral liver infection spread via infected blood, including unsafe blood transfusions, poorly sterilised surgical equipment, reuse of syringes by unqualified practitioners, and unprotected sex. Of the patients registered this year, roughly 4,000 have completed treatment while about 500 remain in care. Treatment centers are located at the government medical college, Nehtaur, and Dhampur, offering free tests and medicines to affected residents.

article.articleHeadline: One in 12 HIV patients in Andhra Pradesh develop tuberculosis again within two years of treatment: Study
article.articleSummary: Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh—A study of 3,357 people living with HIV who completed TB treatment (2017–2021) across East Godavari, Krishna and Guntur found 270 (8%) developed recurrent TB within two years, and 510 (15.2%) died by Dec 31, 2023. Median times: seven months to recurrent TB and eight months to death; 43.7% of recurrences occurred within six months, 67% within 12 months. Unsuppressed HIV viral load (≥1,000 copies/ml) increased adjusted hazards: 3.36 for recurrent TB and 3.71 for death. Not on dolutegravir-based ART yielded 2.62-fold higher hazard of recurrent TB and 2.77-fold higher hazard of death. TB preventive therapy uptake was limited: 43% started within nine months, 35.7% did not receive it. National guidelines call for follow-up at six, 12, 18 and 24 months post-treatment. Findings published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases; limitations include district scope and inability to distinguish relapse vs reinfection.

article.articleHeadline: Pooled Indian data show pneumococcal serotypes and resistance patterns
article.articleSummary: Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype distribution and antimicrobial resistance in India were assessed through a meta-analysis of 26 studies (2007–2024; 4,253 isolates), largely reflecting the pre‑UIP era. Data were stratified into invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD), carriage, and CAP. Pediatric IPD most frequent serotypes: 14 (14.15%), 19F (11.39%), 6B (10.17%); exploratory single‑study data suggested higher estimates for serogroups 6 (25%), 18 (12.5%), 19 (10%). In adult IPD, serotype 1 (11.69%), 23F (6.84%), 19F (6.71%); adult CAP serotypes: 19A (14%), 8 (10%). Cotrimoxazole resistance was highest across contexts: pediatric IPD 86.16%, adult IPD 85.24%, adult CAP 74%. Penicillin non‑susceptibility in pediatric IPD estimated at 14.33% (CI 5.22–33.72) with high heterogeneity (I2 97.15%). PCV20 had the highest serotype coverage; PCV13 remains highly protective though non‑vaccine serotypes are rising. Limitations include pre‑UIP dominance, reliance on small single studies, and substantial heterogeneity, underscoring the need for broad, ongoing surveillance to guide vaccination policy in India.

article.articleHeadline: Keralam measles outbreaks call for a relook at disease epidemiology
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreaks in Keralam state, across Kozhikode, Malappuram and Palakkad, with 824 confirmed and 1,681 probable cases as of 6 November 2026; five measles-related deaths (one confirmed). The disease now affects broader age groups, including fully vaccinated individuals and infants under nine months. UIP vaccination history: introduced 1985, first dose at nine months, second dose at 18 months since 2010; first-dose MR ~95% coverage, second-dose ~85–88%; outbreaks persist amid incomplete immunisation. Experts call for updated epidemiology, possible additional UIP dose in adolescence or before marriage, and serological studies in adolescents and young women. Mumbai 2023 data show infants affected and maternal antibody gaps; RGCB/JAMA Network Open (Aug 2025) found 8.5% of children lacked protective antibodies, 13% IgM+, 63.6% with a third dose, suggesting breakthrough infections and waning immunity; larger epidemiological investigations are needed to identify drivers.

He spoke at a high-level malaria-elimination meeting in Gaborone, Botswana, noting plans to create a national mosquito-net production factory, due to be commissioned next year. Since 2017, Angola has built 735 health facilities nationwide, about 80% of which are primary health-care units, aimed at strengthening the health system and improving access. The roundtable included representatives from Mozambique, Tanzania, Zambia, and Equatorial Guinea. Botswana’s ALMA president Duma Boko stressed the need for stronger political and institutional commitment, higher domestic funding, robust health systems, and strategic partnerships to accelerate malaria elimination across Africa.

article.articleHeadline: The First China–Africa Public Health Forum Successfully Held — Building a New Line of Defense for Sino-African Infectious Disease Prevention and Control
article.articleSummary: China CDC and Africa CDC jointly hosted the first China–Africa Public Health Forum in Guangzhou, November 6–7, 2026, drawing 700 participants from more than 20 African countries, plus UNICEF, WHO, UNAIDS, UNFPA, the African Medicines Agency, PATH, CHAI, ASLM, and Africa Laboratory Professionals Association, as well as domestic institutions. The forum theme was Building a new line of defense for Sino-African infectious disease prevention and control and advancing the China–Africa Health Partnership Action. Topics covered global infectious disease challenges, surveillance, diagnostics and vaccine innovation; improving access to public health products, local production, tropical diseases, tuberculosis, and sexually transmitted infections. China CDC, Africa CDC, and UNICEF launched the Public Health Technical Assistance Project and a South-South Cooperation Program, and issued the China–Africa Initiative to strengthen pathogen detection, surveillance, emergency response, and public health workforce development, with local diagnostic validation. The event strengthens Sino-African health cooperation and Africa's public health resilience.

article.articleHeadline: Lidong Meets El Niño: Nanning's Damp, Cold, and Changeable Weather Leads to High Incidence of Four Types of Diseases
article.articleSummary: In Nanning, during Lidong, El Niño-driven temperature swings and damp-cold conditions raise risks across four disease groups. Cardiovascular: hypertension and coronary heart disease risk increases with rapid temperature changes; patients should monitor blood pressure and avoid stopping medications without a clinician. Respiratory: humid, cold weather favors colds, influenza, and COPD flares. Gastrointestinal: norovirus season brings stomach pain and diarrhea linked to cold exposure and heavy, spicy meals. Musculoskeletal: old rheumatic pain may recur. Prevention emphasizes warming up before cold air, layering clothing to protect the neck, abdomen, and feet, and limiting outdoor activity in cold, damp spells; midday or afternoon exercise is preferred to avoid excessive sweating. Chronic patients should maintain medications and seek care for chest tightness or persistent cough. Traditional Chinese medicine advises nourishing the spleen and removing dampness; consult a clinician before herbal remedies. Increase sunlight exposure to boost mood.

article.articleHeadline: Limited Environmental Links Found to Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis in Eastern
article.articleSummary: Drug-resistant tuberculosis incidence in Pudong New Area, Shanghai, China, from January 2019 through December 2023 (60 monthly observations) averaged 0.053 cases per 100,000 population per month. The ecological time-series study assessed 13 ambient environmental exposures (air pollutants and meteorological factors) for lagged and interactive associations using quasi-Poisson models with single-lag (0–3 months) and distributed-lag (0–6 months) frameworks, time spline and annual sine/cosine terms; heteroskedasticity-robust covariance estimates and Benjamini-Hochberg correction were applied. Lagged associations were heterogeneous and largely non-significant after correction. Relative-humidity showed model-dependent effects, with a cumulative RR of 0.894 (95% CI 0.362–2.209) for 90th vs 50th percentile, not significant post-correction. Bootstrap random forests identified PM10, relative humidity, precipitation, ozone, and sulfur dioxide as top predictors, explaining 52.2% of total importance; joint/interactions were non-significant after correction. The study calls for longer-term, individual-level exposure data to clarify potential environmental influences on DR-TB.

article.articleHeadline: Atypical Toxoplasma gondii Genotypes Cause Fatal Infections in Captive
article.articleSummary: Fatal infections by atypical Toxoplasma gondii genotypes ToxoDB #15 and #169 in two captive primates at a Guangdong Province zoo, China, with deaths occurring between 2024 and 2025. The red-backed bearded saki (Chiropotes chiropotes) and a mandrill suffered rapid disseminated toxoplasmosis without prior signs. Necropsy showed diffuse multi-organ vascular damage, edema, and scattered petechiae; histology revealed acute diffuse inflammation with dense tachyzoite burdens in the saki’s lungs, spleen, and liver and in the mandrill’s myocardium, lungs, and intestinal mucosa. Serology detected anti-Toxoplasma IgG titers of 1:32 (saki heart fluid) and 1:128 (mandrill heart fluid), consistent with seropositivity. Molecular confirmation via TOX-5/TOX-8 PCR detected TgMonkeyGd2 (ToxoDB #15) and TgMonkeyGd3 (ToxoDB #169); viable isolates were recovered in interferon-gamma knockout mice and CV-1 cells. Genotyping across ten loci (SAG1, SAG2, SAG3, BTUB, GRA6, c22-8, c29-2, L358, PK1, Apico) matched TgMonkeyGd2 to ToxoDB #15 and TgMonkeyGd3 to #169; virulence determinants ROP18 4/3 and ROP5 2/3 were identified. This marks the first Asia documentation of these atypical genotypes; hypotheses include recrudescence of latent infection or subclinical primary infection. Negative retrospective virology (SIV, SRV, STLV, hepatitis B).

article.articleHeadline: Delamanid Resistance Emerges Rarely During Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: China conducted a prospective multicenter cohort across ten centers (Beijing Chest Hospital; Hangzhou Red Cross Hospital; Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region Chest Hospital; Chengdu Public Health Clinical Center; Henan Provincial Chest Hospital; Jiangxi Chest Hospital; Kunming Third People's Hospital; Infectious Disease Hospital of Heilongjiang Province; Changsha Central Hospital; Guiyang Public Health Treatment Center) to evaluate delamanid resistance in 263 culture-confirmed MDR/RR-TB patients treated with delamanid-containing regimens between 2020 and 2024. Primary delamanid resistance was detected in 0.76% of tested isolates. Among 263 patients who completed therapy, 187 had favorable outcomes (71.1%) and 76 unfavorable (28.9%). Baseline isolates were largely susceptible to delamanid, and acquired resistance during treatment was extraordinarily rare, supporting the durability of delamanid in MDR-TB regimens. Globally, TB affected about 10.8 million people in 2024 with 1.25 million deaths; China’s MDR-TB burden remains substantial, with 66% treatment success.

article.articleHeadline: A virus found in one out of ten patients in China is carried by a tick species that is spreading across the US
article.articleSummary: ALTNV, an Asian longhorned tick-borne orthonairovirus, was identified in China among 3,163 febrile patients; 328 (10.4%) tested positive for ALTNV by PCR or IgM. ALTNV was detected in ticks from 15 Chinese provinces, with the Asian longhorned tick Haemaphysalis longicornis carrying it most often (1.75% of tested ticks; overall ALTNV in ticks 1.29%). Among ALTNV-alone infections (n=56), fatigue (84%), GI symptoms (80%), thrombocytopenia (38%), and elevated aminotransferases (36%) were common; all recovered without lasting effects. Coinfection with the SFTS-causing Dabie bandavirus (DBV) in 38 patients correlated with more severe disease: respiratory symptoms 61% vs 38% in DBV-only; kidney impairment 84% vs 66%; deaths 7 (18.4%). Recommendations: enhanced testing to distinguish ALTNV from DBV; expanded tick surveillance; note tick vector also spreading in the United States, with New Jersey reported 2017 and 21 states by Oct 2025.

article.articleHeadline: WHO collaborating center inaugurated in south China to aid global sexually transmitted infection control
article.articleSummary: WHO collaborating Center for STI Prevention and Innovations inaugurated in Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, to aid global sexually transmitted infection control. Hosted by the Dermatology Hospital of Southern Medical University and SMU Institute for Global Health, the center will advance capacity building for venereal disease prevention in low- and middle-income countries. Led by Yang Bin, it will pursue standardized training, targeting the creation by 2030 of 100 senior STI professionals across 15 LMICs, prioritizing Africa and Southeast Asia. It will develop simple, standardized data collection tools for STI surveillance, pilot verification in African countries, and build an operational data integration and sharing platform aligned with international systems. Hannah Monica Dias of WHO emphasized guidelines development, evidence generation, and global public health governance support. China-WHO cooperation highlights include 2025 medical personnel deployments and malaria control support in Africa/SE Asia, and pilots of integrated health delivery; Cambodia/Laos schistosomiasis elimination efforts.

article.articleHeadline: Mysterious virus in Croatia kills Dobermans, their eyes turn blue and they die in agony....
article.articleSummary: RFAV (raccoon dog amdoparvovirus), a parvovirus-related infection first identified in wild animals on fur farms in China, has been detected in domestic dogs across Europe, including Croatia, Slovenia, and Bulgaria, with Serbia reporting initial Doberman cases at a facility near Novi Sad. In Croatia, a four-year-old female Doberman Pinscher admitted July 22 to the Zagreb Veterinary Faculty with severe emaciation, purulent ocular discharge, nasal crusting, skin/mucosal jaundice, hepatic damage, and progressive deterioration leading to euthanasia after three days. Laboratory analyses confirmed RFAV infection, with multi-system involvement (eyes, liver, kidneys, nervous system) and blue-eye changes. Serbia’s outbreak traces to late 2025 at a dog-training facility near Novi Sad, where two Russian-imported Dobermans arrived in November 2025; among eight dogs, four Dobermans became ill. Metagenomic sequencing identified the pathogen; transmission route remains unclear, and questions persist about dog-to-dog spread and early diagnosis/treatment.

article.articleHeadline: The peak season for respiratory infectious diseases has arrived! This year, three important changes to watch for in Hunan Province's influenza vaccination program.
article.articleSummary: Influenza persists in Hunan Province during autumn–winter, with dominant A/H3N2 and B Victoria lineage; A/H1N1 detected in small numbers; infection rates highest among 5–14-year-olds. Rhinovirus infections are rising, posing a severe risk to infants; other circulating pathogens include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Respiratory Syncytial Virus, and Haemophilus influenzae type b at typical levels. Three vaccination changes for winter/spring: 1) free influenza vaccination for rural elderly (65+) and rural primary/secondary school students; urban residents can pay via medical insurance accounts for themselves or relatives. 2) priority groups: those at risk of severe disease (60+, chronic disease, under 5, pregnant) and those likely to transmit (healthcare workers, students, childcare workers, elderly-care facility staff, household caregivers). 3) vaccine is trivalent rather than quadrivalent, aligning with Yamagata lineage absence since 2020; WHO recommends this formulation, and protection remains appropriate.

article.articleHeadline: Couple Both Diagnosed; Reminder: Early Symptoms Resemble a Cold
article.articleSummary: In Ningbo's Fenghua District, Zhejiang Province, China, a husband and wife were diagnosed with psittacosis after buying a parrot for 800 yuan. The husband, after five–six days of keeping the bird, developed 39°C fever with headache, myalgia and dry cough; chest CT showed a pulmonary infiltrate, and laboratory tests confirmed Chlamydia psittaci infection. A week later, the wife developed similar illness and was likewise diagnosed; both recovered after treatment. Doctors explained there was no human-to-human transmission in this case; rather, the bird continued to shed the pathogen, releasing aerosolized particles at home, leading to inhalation exposure. Psittacosis is a zoonosis carried by parrots and other birds (pigeons, canaries, chickens, ducks) with respiratory secretions and droppings as sources. Prevention focuses on personal protection (mask, gloves), hand hygiene, cage sanitation, disinfection, food/water safeguards, and regular health monitoring for birds and owners.

article.articleHeadline: Bantul Has the Highest Number of Leptospirosis Cases in DIY: Here Is the Distribution of 576 Cases
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis in Indonesia’s Special Administrative Region of Yogyakarta (DIY) recorded 576 cases and 23 deaths in 2026, with Bantul highest at 250 cases and 9 deaths (data through July 2026). Sleman followed with 196 cases (2 deaths; through Oct 2026), Kulon Progo 61 cases (7 deaths; through Oct 2026), Kota Yogyakarta 34 cases (2 deaths; through Aug 2026), and Gunungkidul 35 cases (3 deaths; through July 2026). The disease is caused by Leptospira bacteria, transmitted from animals—primarily rats—via urine that contaminates water, mud, and soil. Incubation is 2–14 days, occasionally up to 30 days. The most affected age group is 46–64 years. High-risk factors include geography and farming/labor near rivers and irrigation channels; delayed health-seeking worsens outcomes. Prevention: PHBS, handwashing, PPE (boots, gloves), wound care, rodent control, environmental sanitation. Seek medical care promptly if symptoms appear.

article.articleHeadline: Foot-and-mouth disease cases in Bantul drop drastically, 51 cattle exposed in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) in Bantul Regency, Indonesia, shows a sharp decline in 2026. From January through October, 51 cattle were exposed to FMD, and all have recovered as of early November 2026; there were also deaths in prior waves but far fewer recently. In the December 2024 to January 2025 period, 283 cattle contracted FMD, with 32 dead, 2 culled, and 249 still sick. DKPP Bantul intensified vaccination, meeting a 27,500-dose target for 2026 (100% realized). Vaccination eligibility depends on animal health status and pregnancy; not all animals can be vaccinated. The program targets cattle, goats, sheep, and buffalo, delivered through 10 Puskeswan centers serving 17 kapanewon (districts). Vaccines are free from the Ministry of Agriculture, with vaccination offered at farm sites or at Puskeswan facilities to sustain the downward trend.

article.articleSummary: 154 laboratory-confirmed mpox (monkeypox) cases were enrolled from 14 clinics in Thailand, in a study by Chulalongkorn Hospital and the Center for Emerging Infectious Diseases in Clinical Medicine, published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases (October 2026). The cohort was predominantly male (152/154, 98.7%), with a median age of 35 (IQR 28–41); 86.4% identified as men who have sex with men, 5.6% bisexual, and 1.3% heterosexual. Most cases were mild; hospitalizations were limited. Common nonspecific symptoms included fever (37.7%), myalgia (19.6%), cough (8.4%), sore throat (15.6%), and lymphadenopathy (10.4%). Skin/mucosal lesions occurred in 71.4%, notably perianal/genital rashes in 94 cases (61.0%). Some exhibited conjunctivitis, rhinorrhea, oral ulcers, dysphagia, vomiting, or diarrhea (42.6%). Genomic data show initial imports with subsequent domestic transmission and ongoing import/export, with viral adaptation via immune-modulator and replication mutations. Tecovirimat for mpox clade IIb appeared ineffective in the STOMP study.

article.articleHeadline: What is 'Anthrax'? A serious zoonotic disease transmitted from animals to humans. Initial symptoms revealed.
article.articleSummary: Anthrax (Bacillus anthracis) is a serious zoonotic disease reported in Thailand with sporadic occurrences in Don Tan, Mukdahan; Tak; Kanchanaburi; Phitsanulok; Chiang Mai; and Phichit, though not widespread. It persists via durable soil spores and can contaminate livestock and pets. Animals susceptible include cattle, buffalo, goats, and sheep; pigs, horses, dogs, and cats can also be infected, often after consuming raw carcasses. In humans, three forms are described: cutaneous—initial pain, swelling, and a black central eschar from handling contaminated meat; ingestion—abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, fever, anorexia, sometimes bloody stool; inhalational—respiratory symptoms with fever, sore throat, dry cough, progressing to breathing difficulty and rapid death. Prevention stresses avoiding contact with infected animals or carcasses, PPE when exposure risk exists, thorough hand and tool cleaning, and ensuring safe, well-cooked meat. Notify veterinary authorities if unusual animal deaths occur.

article.articleHeadline: Clearing up the doubts: Does sitting on a public toilet put you at risk of monkeypox? Dr. Anant has the answer.
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) transmission via public toilet seats is described as very unlikely but theoretically possible. A Thai health expert notes that Mpox, an Orthopoxvirus, can survive on dry surfaces at room temperature for hours to days, with live virus detected on toilet-seat surfaces in patient bathrooms. However, intact skin provides a strong barrier, making direct sitting transmission unlikely. WHO data indicate mpox infections almost always arise from close physical contact with lesions or with items that retain crusts and moisture (e.g., towels, bed linens). Transmission through hard surfaces like toilet seats has few confirmed reports as a main route. To minimize residual risk, clean the seat with 70% alcohol or disinfectant wipes before use and wash hands with soap after bathroom use; these measures can destroy the viral envelope and prevent infection.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Ghana introduces mandatory health declaration for travellers
article.articleSummary: Ebola, amid heightened outbreaks in parts of Africa, drives Ghana Health Service to impose a mandatory Health Declaration Form for all travellers arriving in Ghana. Effective 12 November 2026, passengers must complete the online form before departure at https://ehds.ghs.gov.gh/declaration. The measure aims to strengthen public health surveillance, improve monitoring of potential health risks, and support early detection and prompt reporting of suspected infectious diseases. Airlines, travel agencies, and other stakeholders are urged to inform passengers and ensure form completion prior to travel. Dr Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, Director-General of the Ghana Health Service, stated the directive safeguards the health and well-being of residents and visitors. The move forms part of broader efforts to bolster cross-border surveillance amid ongoing Ebola concerns in Africa.

article.articleHeadline: Veterinary Officer appeals for support to curb rabies amid rising deaths in Bongo
article.articleSummary: Rabies remains a major threat in Bongo District, Upper East Region, Ghana, with 5 deaths in Bongo and 36 rabies-related deaths region-wide from June 2025 to Sept 2026. Bongo District Veterinary Officer Hamidu Sadat appealed for District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF) support to enable free mass dog vaccination. He linked rising deaths to cross-border dog movements from Burkina Faso via the Yelwongo market, with dogs sold into Bolgatanga and Bongo Soe; many escaped and became strays. The district estimates 3,000–4,000 dogs, yet only 120 vaccine doses were available in the last vaccination exercise, far from sufficient. He noted fear of the GHS 1,000 cost for anti-rabies vaccines deters bite victims from seeking care; drone-delivered vaccines for bite victims have been halted due to stock shortages. He urged sustained dog vaccination, better border monitoring, and prompt bite treatment to reduce human exposure and deaths.

article.articleHeadline: Australia's 'whooping cough corridor' revealed
article.articleSummary: Eight coastal areas from New South Wales’ Richmond River Coast and Tweed Valley to Queensland’s Noosa Hinterland, plus Sydney’s Dural-Wisemans Ferry and the Gold Coast region, are among Australia’s bottom 10 for one-year-old pertussis vaccination, with coverage up to 35% lower than the best areas, according to the Immunisation Foundation of Australia’s 2026 Whooping Cough Report Card. Affected Queensland sites include Coolangatta, Gold Coast Hinterland, Nambour, Maroochy, Noosa and Noosa Hinterland; New South Wales sites include the Richmond River Coast and Tweed Valley; Sydney’s Dural-Wisemans Ferry; and Western Australia’s Gascoyne region. With warmer months and summer holidays approaching, whooping cough infections are expected to surge, and families travelling with babies are urged to check vaccination status. One-year-olds up to date with vaccination have fallen below 90% for the first time in over 25 years. Whooping cough is highly contagious and causes prolonged coughing fits, and can be life-threatening for young infants.
